::: {.eyebrow}
Therapy
:::

Two methods: **MBMR** (this page) and the broader
[(Re-)Synchronising Therapy Method (STM)](stm.qmd), in which MBMR forms the
physical backbone.

![](../assets/therapy/river-forest.jpg){.therapy-hero fig-alt=""}

## What MBMR is

A specific model of bilateral movement therapy for traumatic memories, whose
central mechanism is the alternation of states of consciousness across two
modalities: 1. Time ('present', 'past', 'future') and 2. Object of attention
('internal stimulus', 'external stimulus', 'stimulus-free').

## The two modalities

The alternation runs along two axes. Each session moves the client's attention
through the nine combinations these axes span together.

::: {layout-ncol=2}
::: {.card .p-4}
#### 1 · Time

- present
- past
- future
:::

::: {.card .p-4}
#### 2 · Object of attention

- internal stimulus
- external stimulus
- stimulus-free
:::
:::

## Who it is for

The method is used for:

- Trauma / PTSD
- Anxiety and panic
- Burn-out and overstrain
- Depressive complaints
- Grief and loss
- Chronic stress
- Physical tension complaints
- Personal development (no complaint)

## Practical

A 60-minute intake, in which psychodiagnostic assessment establishes the
'avidya' and 'dukkha' values using the assessment I developed. A movement therapy
programme follows — for example Mindful Running Therapy (MHT) — running eight
weeks, twice a week, with 90-minute sessions in a fixed format of my own design.

| | |
|---|---|
| Intake | 60 minutes, with psychodiagnostic assessment |
| Programme | 8 weeks, 2 sessions per week |
| Session length | 90 minutes, fixed format |
| Example | Mindful Running Therapy (MHT) |
